alice.name: cogmem_consolidate
alice.description: Ask the background process to review the recent conversation and update memory now. Returns immediately; the work runs in the background.

alice.name: cogmem_domain_archive
alice.description: Archive a domain so it is no longer used in prompting.

alice.name: cogmem_domain_create
alice.description: Create a new memory domain and return its assigned id. A domain groups related memories; register each ongoing project/topic as its own domain. Names must be unique — creating one with an existing name returns an error (reuse or rename instead).

keyword_triggers.description: Optional keyword triggers: words/phrases that load this domain when they appear in the incoming message (whole-phrase, word-boundary). Prefer multi-word phrases like "morning routine"; common words are rejected. Use this to pull a workflow's context up when a cron job fires.

sticky.description: true = always inject this domain into context every turn (use sparingly). Default false: loaded only when relevant.

triggers.description: Optional tool triggers: comma-separated name fragments that auto-load this domain whenever you use a tool whose name contains one (substring, case-insensitive). E.g. "mail,github"; for an MCP server use its name ("github" matches mcp_github_*).

alice.name: cogmem_domain_get
alice.description: Load a domain by id, with its active memories as readable text (each memory's id included).

alice.name: cogmem_domain_list
alice.description: List memory domains (id, name, summary, status; sticky ones are marked). Optionally filter by status. To see everything you're tracking, list with no filter.

alice.name: cogmem_domain_migrate
alice.description: Merge two domains: move every memory from the 'from' domain into the 'to' domain, then permanently delete the 'from' domain. Use this to consolidate duplicate/overlapping domains into one.

from.description: Source domain id — its memories are moved out and the domain is deleted.

to.description: Destination domain id — receives the moved memories.

alice.name: cogmem_domain_update
alice.description: Update a domain — a patch: pass only the fields you want to change (rename, summary, state, sticky, triggers). No version needed.

set_keyword_triggers.description: Replace keyword triggers: words/phrases that load this domain when they appear in the incoming message (whole-phrase, word-boundary). This is the full list domain_get shows, including keyword triggers added automatically; leave one out to remove it. Prefer multi-word phrases like "morning routine"; common words are rejected. Empty list clears.

set_name.description: Rename the domain. Names must be unique; rejected if another domain already uses it.

set_sticky.description: true = always inject this domain into context every turn; false = routed only when relevant. Use sticky sparingly.

set_triggers.description: Replace tool triggers: comma-separated name fragments that auto-load this domain whenever you use a tool whose name contains one (substring, case-insensitive). E.g. "mail,github"; for an MCP server use its name ("github" matches mcp_github_*). Empty string clears.

alice.name: cogmem_explain
alice.description: Summarize the status, origin, and evidence of a domain or memory id.

id.description: A domain id (d…) or memory id (h…).

alice.name: cogmem_export
alice.description: Dump the agent's entire memory — every domain and memory, with all their fields — to files/MEMORY_EXPORT.yaml, and report the path and counts. The format can be read back in, so it works as a backup or to hand your memory to another assistant.

alice.name: cogmem_memory_attach
alice.description: Attach a markdown file to an existing memory, or detach the current one. The attached file's FULL contents load into your context whenever that memory does. Use this to point a memory at a different document (e.g. the file moved or was rewritten) or to remove the document while keeping the memory — memory text itself is not editable; retire and re-create for that.

file.description: Path to a markdown file you can read with the file tools (e.g. "files/voice.md", "maestro/style-guide.md"). Omit or pass an empty string to detach the current file.

alice.name: cogmem_memory_create
alice.description: Record a memory. With NO domain_id and NO domain_hint it records to your sticky 'General' domain (always in context). Give a domain_hint to use (or create) a topic domain by name, or a domain_id to target a specific one. Choose the type carefully — it decides whether the memory is in your context every turn or only reachable by search.

domain_hint.description: A domain name: an existing domain with that name is reused, otherwise a new (non-sticky) one is created. Omit to use General.

domain_id.description: Target domain id. If omitted and no domain_hint is given, records to the sticky General domain.

file.description: Optional path to a markdown file (e.g. "files/voice.md", "maestro/style-guide.md") whose FULL contents are injected into your context whenever this memory is in context. Use it for reference material too long to put in the memory text, such as a writing-voice description; keep the memory text as a one-line description of what the document is and when to use it. The path must be one you can read with the file tools, and the file is read fresh each turn.

type.description: fact = something true that stays true. preference = how the user likes things done. rule = a hard directive governing your output or behaviour toward the user. operational = your OWN housekeeping: where you file things, how you work, a rule you set for your own method. event = something that happened at a point in time (a trip, a delivery, a scheduled run, a status as of a date). Use event for anything with a timestamp or that will be stale next week — events are NEVER loaded into your context and are reached only by memory_search, which is what keeps recurring notes from crowding out everything else.

alice.name: cogmem_memory_forget
alice.description: Retire all active memories matching a query (optionally limited to one domain). Reports how many were retired.

query.description: Substring to match against active memory text.

alice.name: cogmem_memory_retire
alice.description: Retire a memory so it is no longer used (it stays in the audit history). To change a memory, retire the old one and create a new one.

alice.name: cogmem_memory_search
alice.description: Search your active memories by a word or phrase in their text (case-insensitive). Use it to look something up when the answer may be in memory but is not currently shown in your context. Event memories are excluded unless you pass include_events — they are never in your context, so search is the ONLY way to reach them.

include_events.description: Include event memories (things that happened at a point in time: trips, deliveries, scheduled runs). Default false. Set true when the question is about the past — "when did we last…", "what happened on…".

query.description: Word or phrase to match against memory text.

alice.name: cogmem_status
alice.description: Report memory status: database path, the last background update, and how many domains and memories are held.

alice.name: file_list
alice.description: See what is in a folder: lists its files and subfolders, one level by default; recursive=true lists the whole tree. To find files by name, use file_glob.

path.description: Path to list

recursive.description: List the entire tree under path (paths shown relative to the workspace). Hidden directories are skipped. Default false (one level).

alice.name: file_read_lines
alice.description: Read the lines you found: reads a file by line number from `start_line` (1-based; a line number from file_search_lines) for `line_count` lines. Lines come back numbered and the status block gives the next `start_line`. Use it to get the exact text before file_edit. (To page by raw bytes instead, use file_read_bytes.)

line_count.description: Number of lines to read from start_line (default 250). Still capped to the byte limit.

path.description: Path to the file to read.

alice.name: get_tool_details
alice.description: Show the full input schema of a tool found via search_tools. Pass the exact tool name from the search results.

name.description: Exact tool name from search_tools results.

alice.name: maestro_file_append
alice.description: Append content to a file in a project or playbook. If the file exists, content is added to the end; otherwise it is created. Reference is read-only.

path.description: File path within the domain

alice.name: maestro_file_convert
alice.description: Convert files in a project to Markdown. Supports PDF, DOCX, and XLSX files. Project files only.

path.description: Path within project files directory. Must be a file if recursive=false, or a directory if recursive=true.

recursive.description: If true, recursively convert all files in directory. If false, convert single file. Default: false.

alice.name: maestro_file_copy
alice.description: Copy a file within or between domains (reference, playbooks, projects). More efficient than using get+put as it doesn't load file content into the conversation. Use this instead of get+put when copying files.

from_playbook.description: Source playbook name (required when from_source is 'playbook')

from_project.description: Source project name (required when from_source is 'project')

summary.description: Optional summary description for the destination file metadata

to_playbook.description: Destination playbook name (required when to_source is 'playbook')

to_project.description: Destination project name (required when to_source is 'project')

alice.name: maestro_file_delete
alice.description: Delete a file from a project or playbook domain. Reference is read-only and cannot be deleted from.

path.description: File path to delete

alice.name: maestro_file_edit
alice.description: Edit a file in a project or playbook using search-and-replace. The old_string must exist in the file exactly as specified. If it appears multiple times, use replace_all=true. Reference is read-only.

new_string.description: Text to replace it with (can be empty string to delete)

old_string.description: Exact text to find and replace (must exist in file)

path.description: File path within the domain

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences (default: false - fails if old_string appears multiple times)

alice.name: maestro_file_extract
alice.description: Extract a zip archive within a project's files directory. Extracts to a directory with the same name as the archive (without .zip extension) in the same location. Project files only.

convert.description: If true, convert extracted files (PDF, DOCX, XLSX) to Markdown after extraction. Default: false.

overwrite.description: If true, overwrite existing files during extraction. Default: false (skip existing files).

path.description: Path to the .zip file within the project files directory

alice.name: maestro_file_get
alice.description: Read a file from a project, playbook, or reference domain. The reference domain (source="reference") holds Maestro's built-in guidance - new to Maestro? Call start_here (or read 'start.md'), then explore 'phases/'. Note: to copy a file, use file_copy instead of get+put - it's more efficient and doesn't load content into the conversation.

byte_offset.description: Byte position to start reading from, for chunked reading of large files (default: 0)

max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes to return in this chunk, for chunked reading of large files (default: 0 = entire file)

path.description: File path within the domain

alice.name: maestro_file_import
alice.description: Import external files into a project's files/imported/ directory. This bypasses the normal chroot restrictions to allow importing files from anywhere on the filesystem. Imported files can then be accessed via the file_* tools with source="project".

convert.description: If true, automatically convert imported files (PDF, DOCX, XLSX) to Markdown after import.

project.description: Target project name to import files into

recursive.description: If true, recursively import directories. Required when source is a directory.

source.description: Source file or directory path (absolute). Only paths this agent may already read — its workspace, its mounts and its allowed read paths — can be imported; anything else is refused.

alice.name: maestro_file_list
alice.description: List files in a project, playbook, or reference domain.

alice.name: maestro_file_put
alice.description: Create or update a file in a project or playbook. Reference is read-only. Note: to copy a file, use file_copy instead of get+put - it's more efficient and doesn't load content into the conversation.

path.description: File path within the domain

alice.name: maestro_file_rename
alice.description: Rename or move a file within a project or playbook. Reference is read-only.

alice.name: maestro_file_search
alice.description: Search files by filename or content in a project, playbook, or reference domain. Omit the owner name to search all within the domain.

playbook.description: Playbook name (optional when source is 'playbook'; searches all if omitted)

project.description: Project name (optional when source is 'project'; searches all if omitted)

alice.name: maestro_health
alice.description: Check Maestro health status. Returns whether the system is healthy and any issues that need to be resolved (e.g. a missing base directory). When the host owns LLM dispatch, no LLM configuration is reported.

alice.name: maestro_list_copy
alice.description: Copy a list from one location to another. Supports copying between projects, playbooks, and reference (source only).

sample.description: Randomly sample N items from the source list instead of copying all. Useful for test audits.

alice.name: maestro_list_create
alice.description: Create a new list. Lists cannot be created in the reference domain.

alice.name: maestro_list_create_tasks
alice.description: Create tasks from list items. Creates one task per item with item context appended to the prompt.

instructions_file.description: Path to instructions file. For 'playbook' source, path MUST start with playbook name: 'playbook-name/path/file.md'. For 'project' source (uses target project) or 'reference' source, use relative path: 'path/file.md'.

instructions_file_source.description: Source type for instructions_file: 'project' (default - uses project's files directory), 'playbook' (uses playbook files), or 'reference' (uses embedded reference docs).

list_playbook.description: Playbook containing the list (when list_source is 'playbook')

list_project.description: Project containing the list (when list_source is 'project')

list_source.description: Source domain for the list: 'project' (default), 'playbook', or 'reference'

llm_model_id.description: Optional model hint for the worker, passed to the host: one of the host agent's configured model aliases. Leave empty to use the host's default model. Unknown aliases fail the task without retry.

parallel.description: Enable parallel task execution. Set to true if tasks are independent and can run concurrently for efficiency. Default: false (sequential).

path.description: Task set path for created tasks (e.g., 'analysis', 'analysis/code')

priority.description: Task priority for all created tasks

prompt.description: Base prompt (item context will be appended)

qa_enabled.description: Enable QA phase for this task

qa_llm_model_id.description: Optional model hint for QA, passed to the host: one of the host agent's configured model aliases. Leave empty to use the host's default model. Unknown aliases fail the task without retry.

sample.description: Randomly sample N items from the list instead of using all items. Useful for test audits.

title_template.description: Task title template. Use {{title}} for item title, {{id}} for item ID. Default: '{{title}}'

type.description: Task type for all created tasks

alice.name: maestro_list_delete
alice.description: Delete a list. Lists cannot be deleted from the reference domain.

alice.name: maestro_list_get
alice.description: Get the full contents of a list including all items.

alice.name: maestro_list_get_summary
alice.description: Get list metadata with paginated items (content truncated to 100 chars).

complete.description: Filter by complete status (projects only): 'true', 'false', or '' (no filter)

alice.name: maestro_list_item_add
alice.description: Add a new item to a list. Item IDs are auto-generated.

content.description: Full item content (used for task execution)

alice.name: maestro_list_item_get
alice.description: Get a single item from a list by ID.

alice.name: maestro_list_item_remove
alice.description: Remove an item from a list.

alice.name: maestro_list_item_rename
alice.description: Rename an item's ID. The new ID must be unique within the list.

alice.name: maestro_list_item_search
alice.description: Search for items in a list. Query matches id or content (case-insensitive). All filters are ANDed.

complete.description: Filter by complete status (projects only): 'true', 'false', or '' (no filter)

query.description: Search query (matches id or content, case-insensitive)

alice.name: maestro_list_item_update
alice.description: Update an existing item in a list. Only specified fields are updated.

clear_tags.description: Set to true to clear all tags

complete.description: Mark item as complete (true) or incomplete (false). Cannot be set to true for playbook lists.

alice.name: maestro_list_list
alice.description: List all lists in the specified source (project, playbook, or reference).

alice.name: maestro_list_rename
alice.description: Rename a list. Lists cannot be renamed in the reference domain.

alice.name: maestro_playbook_create
alice.description: Create a new playbook.

alice.name: maestro_playbook_delete
alice.description: Delete a playbook and all its files.

alice.name: maestro_playbook_list
alice.description: List all playbooks. Playbooks are user-created collections of reusable knowledge and procedures.

alice.name: maestro_playbook_rename
alice.description: Rename a playbook.

alice.name: maestro_project_create
alice.description: Create a new project with metadata.

context.description: Global context included in all task prompts (e.g., audit period, customer info)

disclaimer_template.description: Path to disclaimer file for reports (e.g., 'playbook-name/templates/disclaimer.md') or 'none'. This text appears at the top of generated reports. Use it to disclose AI assistance.

alice.name: maestro_project_delete
alice.description: Delete a project and all its contents.

alice.name: maestro_project_get
alice.description: Get project metadata including tasks.

alice.name: maestro_project_list
alice.description: List all projects.

limit.description: Maximum number of projects to return

alice.name: maestro_project_log_append
alice.description: Append a message to a project log.

alice.name: maestro_project_log_get
alice.description: Get log entries from a project.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return

alice.name: maestro_project_rename
alice.description: Rename a project.

alice.name: maestro_project_update
alice.description: Update project metadata.

context.description: Global context included in all task prompts (optional)

disclaimer_template.description: Path to disclaimer MD file for reports (optional)

alice.name: maestro_report_create
alice.description: Generate reports from task results. Uses the same report generation logic as the runner. Supports optional path filtering.

path.description: Task set path prefix to filter (optional)

alice.name: maestro_report_get
alice.description: List reports in a project (omit 'report'), or read a specific report (provide 'report'). Reports are generated automatically by the runner.

byte_offset.description: Byte position to start reading from, when reading a report (default: 0)

max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes to return, when reading a report (default: 0 = entire file)

report.description: Report filename to read (e.g., '20251219-1234-Audit-Report.md'). Omit to list all reports.

alice.name: maestro_report_write
alice.description: Write to a project's report session. action='start' begins a session and sets a prefix (e.g., '20251219-1234-Audit-'); action='append' (default) adds content to the active session (auto-initializes if none); action='end' clears the session.

content.description: Content to append in markdown (required when action='append')

intro.description: Optional introductory paragraph written to the main report (action='start')

report.description: Report name suffix for append (optional - omit for main report, e.g., 'Summary' creates <prefix>Summary.md)

title.description: Report title, used to generate the prefix (required when action='start')

alice.name: maestro_start_here
alice.description: CALL THIS FIRST. Returns the Maestro orientation guide. Using Maestro without reading this risks errors and data loss.

alice.name: maestro_supervisor_update
alice.description: Allows a supervisor to replace the worker response with their own content. The response must pass template validation. History is append-only.

response.description: Supervisor's replacement response (must match worker_response_template if defined)

alice.name: maestro_task_create
alice.description: Create a new task within a task set. At least one prompt field is required.

llm_model_id.description: Optional model hint for the worker, passed to the host: one of the host agent's configured model aliases. Leave empty to use the host's default model. Unknown aliases fail the task without retry.

path.description: Task set path

qa_enabled.description: Enable QA phase for this task

qa_llm_model_id.description: Optional model hint for QA, passed to the host: one of the host agent's configured model aliases. Leave empty to use the host's default model. Unknown aliases fail the task without retry.

alice.name: maestro_task_delete
alice.description: Delete a task by UUID.

alice.name: maestro_task_dispatch
alice.description: Create and immediately execute a single task asynchronously. Returns immediately with task UUID and status 'running'. Optionally fires a callback when complete.

instructions_file_source.description: Source for instructions file: project, playbook, or reference

llm_model_id.description: Optional model hint for the worker, passed to the host: one of the host agent's configured model aliases. Leave empty to use the host's default model. Unknown aliases fail the task without retry.

path.description: Taskset path (auto-generated as 'dispatch/<uuid8>' if omitted)

alice.name: maestro_task_get
alice.description: Get a task by UUID or by path and ID.

id.description: Task ID within task set (required with path)

path.description: Task set path (required with id)

alice.name: maestro_task_list
alice.description: List tasks, optionally filtered by path, status, or type.

limit.description: Maximum number of tasks to return

path.description: Task set path to list tasks from (optional, lists all if empty)

status.description: Filter by work status: waiting, processing, done, failed

alice.name: maestro_task_report
alice.description: Generate a report from task results. Supports filtering and multiple output formats.

path.description: Task set path prefix to filter (optional)

alice.name: maestro_task_result_get
alice.description: Get a single task result by UUID. Returns worker/QA responses without history or prompts. Includes worker_response_template for supervisor updates.

alice.name: maestro_task_results
alice.description: Get task execution results. Returns completed task results with their outputs.

path.description: Task set path prefix to filter (optional)

qa_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against QA response (optional). If both patterns provided, uses OR logic.

summary.description: If true, returns only task_id, task_uuid, task_title, work_status (default: false)

task_id.description: Specific task ID to get result for (optional)

worker_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against worker response (optional)

alice.name: maestro_task_run
alice.description: Run eligible tasks for a project. Tasks in 'waiting' or 'retry' status are executed. Returns immediately with count of tasks queued.

parallel.description: Override taskset parallel setting: 'true' or 'false' (optional, defaults to taskset setting)

path.description: Task set path prefix to filter (optional)

alice.name: maestro_task_status
alice.description: Get current status of tasks in a project, including counts by status and whether a run is in progress.

path.description: Task set path prefix to filter (optional)

alice.name: maestro_task_update
alice.description: Update a task's metadata, instructions, or prompts.

instructions_file.description: Path to instructions file (validated before update)

llm_model_id.description: Optional model hint for the worker, passed to the host: one of the host agent's configured model aliases. Leave empty to use the host's default model. Unknown aliases fail the task without retry.

qa_instructions_file.description: Path to QA instructions file (validated before update)

qa_llm_model_id.description: Optional model hint for QA, passed to the host: one of the host agent's configured model aliases. Leave empty to use the host's default model. Unknown aliases fail the task without retry.

work_status.description: New work status (optional): waiting, retry or done. processing, failed and error are set by the runner only. Only the status changes: invocation counts, QA state and the result file are kept, so a task whose work already finished is not re-run. Use taskset_reset to re-run tasks from scratch.

alice.name: maestro_taskset_create
alice.description: Create a new task set at a given path within a project.

parallel.description: Enable parallel task execution. Set to true if tasks are independent and can run concurrently for efficiency. Default: false (sequential).

path.description: Task set path (e.g., 'analysis', 'analysis/code', max 3 levels)

qa_report_template.description: Path to markdown template for QA reports

qa_response_template.description: Path to JSON schema file for QA responses

skip_validation.description: Skip schema validation and report generation for this task set (default: false)

worker_report_template.description: Path to markdown template for worker reports

worker_response_template.description: Path to JSON schema file for worker responses

alice.description: Delete a task set and all its tasks.

alice.name: maestro_taskset_update
alice.description: Update a task set's metadata.

parallel.description: Set parallel execution: 'true' or 'false'. Use true if tasks are independent (optional).

path.description: Task set path

qa_report_template.description: Path to markdown template for QA reports

qa_response_template.description: Path to JSON schema file for QA responses

worker_report_template.description: Path to markdown template for worker reports

worker_response_template.description: Path to JSON schema file for worker responses

alice.name: search_tools
alice.description: Search for available tools by capability. Returns matching tool names with one-line descriptions and makes those tools available: call one directly, or call get_tool_details on a name to see its full schema. Natural-language query by default; set regex:true to match a regular expression if the natural-language search can't find the tool. Discoverable tool groups: maestro.

query.description: What you want to do (natural language), or a regex pattern when regex is true.

regex.description: Treat query as a regex over tool name/description instead of a natural-language search.

alice.name: time_now
alice.description: Get the current date, time, and timezone. The system prompt carries today's date only, so call this whenever you need the time of day, the timezone or UTC offset, or a precise timestamp — for example to work out how long until something, or to convert between zones.

timezone.description: Optional IANA timezone name (e.g. "America/Toronto", "UTC"). Defaults to the server's local timezone.

alice.name: web_search
alice.description: Search the web for current information. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets from search results.

alice.name: wxca_city_current
alice.description: Environment and Climate Change Canada Weather: Get only the compact English current observations for one forecast-location feature ID, such as on-118 or qc-147: temperature, condition, wind direction/speed/gust, wind chill, humidity, dewpoint, pressure, station, observation time, and any active warnings. No forecast is included; use city_get for the 7-day day/night outlook or city_hourly for the next 24 hours.

identifier.description: Weather Canada city-page feature ID returned by city_search or city_list, for example on-118, qc-147, bc-74, or ns-19. (length: 4-32) (pattern: ^[a-z]{2}-[a-z0-9]+$)

alice.name: wxca_city_get
alice.description: Environment and Climate Change Canada Weather: Get a compact English city-page weather record for one forecast-location feature ID, such as on-118 or qc-147. Returns current observations (temperature, condition, wind, gust, humidity, dewpoint, pressure, wind chill, station, observation time) and the official day/night forecast periods covering about seven days (forecast text plus high/low temperatures), with sunrise/sunset and any active warnings. Hourly forecasts are not included here; use city_hourly for those.

identifier.description: Weather Canada city-page feature ID returned by city_search or city_list, for example on-118, qc-147, bc-74, or ns-19. (length: 4-32) (pattern: ^[a-z]{2}-[a-z0-9]+$)

alice.name: wxca_city_list
alice.description: Environment and Climate Change Canada Weather: List Weather Canada city-page locations and their feature IDs. Use this when free-text search is unavailable or when resolving an ambiguous place name. Page with limit and offset, then call city_get with the chosen feature ID.

bbox.description: Optional west,south,east,north bounding box in longitude/latitude. (pattern: ^-?\d+(\.\d+)?,-?\d+(\.\d+)?,-?\d+(\.\d+)?,-?\d+(\.\d+)?$)

alice.name: wxca_city_near_coordinates
alice.description: Environment and Climate Change Canada Weather: Find Weather Canada city-page forecast locations near known coordinates. Supply a small west,south,east,north bounding box around the point. Select the closest returned feature by geometry, then call city_get with its ID.

bbox.description: Required bounding box as west,south,east,north in longitude/latitude. For a point, start with roughly ±0.5 degrees and widen if no location is returned. (pattern: ^-?\d+(\.\d+)?,-?\d+(\.\d+)?,-?\d+(\.\d+)?,-?\d+(\.\d+)?$)

alice.name: wxca_city_schema
alice.description: Environment and Climate Change Canada Weather: Return the current schema for the experimental city-page weather collection. Use this to interpret fields or diagnose upstream schema changes.

alice.name: wxca_city_search
alice.description: Environment and Climate Change Canada Weather: Find Weather Canada city-page forecast locations. Use q for a city or community name when supported by the API. A bbox can instead restrict results geographically. Returns only the feature id, name, region, and coordinates for each match (not the full weather record); pass a selected id to city_get. For ambiguous names, inspect name and region before choosing.

bbox.description: Optional bounding box as west,south,east,north in longitude/latitude (EPSG:4326), for example -75.9,45.2,-75.4,45.6 for the Ottawa area. (pattern: ^-?\d+(\.\d+)?,-?\d+(\.\d+)?,-?\d+(\.\d+)?,-?\d+(\.\d+)?$)

limit.description: Maximum number of matching locations to return. (default: 20) (range: 1-100)

q.description: Free-text location search, such as Ottawa, Montréal, Saint John, or Yellowknife. If the server does not support free-text search for this collection, use bbox or city_list instead.

bob.name: agent_cancel
bob.description: Cancel your own background tasks (sub-agents and task-model calls started with agent_spawn), with the tasks they started. Give 'uuid' for one task, or 'all': true for every running one. A cancelled task sends no result. Returns how many were cancelled and which had already finished.

all.description: Cancel every running task of yours

uuid.description: The task uuid returned by agent_spawn (or shown by agent_list)

bob.name: agent_list
bob.description: List this agent's background tasks. Returns uuid, name, and status for each.

bob.name: agent_message
bob.description: Send a message to another agent. wait_seconds 0 whispers: the message is added privately to the start of the agent's next message, and this returns at once. wait_seconds above 0 asks: the agent handles the message in a normal turn, with its own tools, and this returns its reply (or says it did not reply in time). Only agents in your subagents.allow_agents can be messaged.

agent.description: The agent to message, by id or name

wait_seconds.description: 0 to whisper (no reply); more than 0 to ask and wait up to this many seconds for the reply

bob.name: agent_spawn
bob.description: Spawn a subagent to handle a task. Use 'mode' to choose how it runs: 'callback' (default) runs it in the background and notifies you when done with a pointer to a result file in your workspace (read it with your file tools, or poll agent_status); 'wait' runs it to completion and returns the result immediately. Callback mode requires 'name', a short identifier for the task. 'media' attaches media:// refs (from '[attachment ref(s): …]' markers in the conversation) to the subagent's initial message — useful to hand an image you cannot view to a vision-capable agent or model for analysis. With 'kind' it calls a task model instead of a subagent: one call, no tools, no agent. Kinds: 'text' (write, translate or summarise: 'task' is the prompt, text 'files' are added to it), 'image' (generate, or edit the images in 'files'/'media': 'task' is the prompt), 'tts' (speak 'task' aloud; optional 'voice' and 'format'), 'stt' (transcribe the one audio file in 'files' or 'media'; 'task' is an optional hint). 'model' then names a task model of that kind; omit it to use the first one that works. Output is saved in your workspace under files/generated/<date>/ and the result gives the paths: images and audio come back as paths only, so send one to the chat with msg_send_file; text and transcripts come back inline too, cut when long, with the full text in a .md file. agent_id and character_card can't be used with kind. If your turn is interrupted while it waits, the task goes on and its result arrives later as a background result.

agent_id.description: Optional target agent ID to delegate the task to

character_card.description: Optional character card id from the library: the subagent runs as that character instead of with the agent's own card. The card must exist.

files.description: With kind: workspace paths of input files (text to use, images to edit, the audio to transcribe), as the file tools take them. You must be allowed to read them.

format.description: With kind tts: the audio format in the API's terms (mp3, wav, …). Omit for the model's default.

kind.description: Call a task model instead of a subagent: text, image, tts (speech) or stt (transcription). You must be allowed that kind.

media.description: Optional media:// refs (from '[attachment ref(s): …]' markers in the conversation) to attach to the subagent's initial message. Use with a vision-capable agent_id/model to have an image you cannot view analyzed for you.

model.description: Optional model for the subagent to run, by its model name. Must be one of the executing agent's worker models (yourself on a self-spawn, or the target agent): its configured worker models, else its own models. Omit to use its first worker model. Useful to run a heavier model for a demanding subtask while you stay on a lighter one.

name.description: Short identifier for the task (required for callback mode)

task.description: The task for the subagent to complete

voice.description: With kind tts: the voice. Omit for the model's default.

bob.name: agent_status
bob.description: Check the status of a background task by uuid. Returns one of: unknown, running, done, error, cancelled — with a pointer to the result file when available.

uuid.description: The task uuid returned by agent_spawn (or shown by agent_list)

bob.name: ccv3
bob.description: Manage the character-card library (Character Card V3). A card describes a character an agent can play: who it is, how it speaks, its world. Actions: list; get {id}; create {id, card}; update {id, changes}; rename {id, new_id}; copy {id, new_id}; delete {id}. Ids are 1 to 64 letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter or digit; case does not matter. Fields of card: name (required); nickname; description; personality; scenario; first_mes, alternate_greetings, group_only_greetings (greetings); mes_example (example dialogue, <START> between examples); system_prompt, post_history_instructions (instructions for the model); tags, creator, character_version, source, creator_notes, creator_notes_multilingual (about the card); character_book (lorebook entries: keys, content, enabled, insertion_order); assets, extensions (kept, not used). creation_date and modification_date are set automatically. In card text {{char}} becomes the character's name, {{user}} becomes "the user" and {{// note}} is removed. The schema is strict: unknown fields are refused. changes is an RFC 7386 merge patch: null removes a field, objects merge, arrays are replaced whole. Cards are attached to agents by the operator in the WebUI, by agent_spawn's character_card, or by a forum participant's character_card; an attached card cannot be renamed or deleted.

action.description: list, get, create, update, rename, copy or delete

assets.description: Images and other files the card refers to; kept, not used

ext.description: The file type, such as png

type.description: What the asset is, such as icon or background

character_book.description: The lorebook: background entries about the character and its world

comment.description: A note about the entry; not shown to the model

constant.description: Always use the entry, whatever the keys

enabled.description: Whether the entry is used; required

extensions.description: Data other apps keep with the entry; kept as is

id.description: The entry's id: a whole number or text

insertion_order.description: Lower numbers are placed first; required

keys.description: Words that trigger the entry; required

position.description: Where the entry is placed relative to the character

priority.description: Which entries are dropped first when over budget (lower first)

secondary_keys.description: Further keys, used when selective is true

extensions.description: Data other apps keep with the lorebook; kept as is

recursive_scanning.description: Whether entry content is scanned for further keys

scan_depth.description: How many recent messages are scanned for keys

creation_date.description: Set automatically (Unix seconds); leave it out

creator_notes.description: Notes from the creator for people using the card; not shown to the model

creator_notes_multilingual.description: creator_notes by language code (such as fr)

description.description: Who the character is: appearance, history, situation

extensions.description: Data other apps keep with the card; kept as is

group_only_greetings.description: First messages used only in group chats

mes_example.description: Example dialogue showing how the character speaks; separate examples with <START>

modification_date.description: Set automatically (Unix seconds); leave it out

name.description: The character's name; required, not blank

nickname.description: What the character is called in text; replaces name for {{char}} when set

personality.description: A short summary of the character's personality

post_history_instructions.description: Instructions placed after the conversation history

scenario.description: The circumstances and context of the conversation

source.description: Where the card came from, as a list (such as URLs)

system_prompt.description: Instructions for the model, placed before the character

group_only_greetings.description: First messages used only in group chats

mes_example.description: Example dialogue showing how the character speaks; separate examples with <START>

name.description: The character's name; required, not blank

nickname.description: What the character is called in text; replaces name for {{char}} when set

personality.description: A short summary of the character's personality

post_history_instructions.description: Instructions placed after the conversation history

scenario.description: The circumstances and context of the conversation

source.description: Where the card came from, as a list (such as URLs)

new_id.description: rename and copy: the new card id

bob.name: cogmem_consolidate
bob.description: Ask the background process to review the recent conversation and update memory now. Returns immediately; the work runs in the background.

bob.name: cogmem_domain_archive
bob.description: Archive a domain so it is no longer used in prompting.

bob.name: cogmem_domain_create
bob.description: Create a new memory domain and return its assigned id. A domain groups related memories; register each ongoing project/topic as its own domain. Names must be unique — creating one with an existing name returns an error (reuse or rename instead).

keyword_triggers.description: Optional keyword triggers: words/phrases that load this domain when they appear in the incoming message (whole-phrase, word-boundary). Prefer multi-word phrases like "morning routine"; common words are rejected. Use this to pull a workflow's context up when a cron job fires.

sticky.description: true = always inject this domain into context every turn (use sparingly). Default false: loaded only when relevant.

triggers.description: Optional tool triggers: comma-separated name fragments that auto-load this domain whenever you use a tool whose name contains one (substring, case-insensitive). E.g. "mail,github"; for an MCP server use its name ("github" matches mcp_github_*).

bob.name: cogmem_domain_get
bob.description: Load a domain by id, with its active memories as readable text (each memory's id included).

bob.name: cogmem_domain_list
bob.description: List memory domains (id, name, summary, status; sticky ones are marked). Optionally filter by status. To see everything you're tracking, list with no filter.

bob.name: cogmem_domain_migrate
bob.description: Merge two domains: move every memory from the 'from' domain into the 'to' domain, then permanently delete the 'from' domain. Use this to consolidate duplicate/overlapping domains into one.

from.description: Source domain id — its memories are moved out and the domain is deleted.

to.description: Destination domain id — receives the moved memories.

bob.name: cogmem_domain_update
bob.description: Update a domain — a patch: pass only the fields you want to change (rename, summary, state, sticky, triggers). No version needed.

set_keyword_triggers.description: Replace keyword triggers: words/phrases that load this domain when they appear in the incoming message (whole-phrase, word-boundary). This is the full list domain_get shows, including keyword triggers added automatically; leave one out to remove it. Prefer multi-word phrases like "morning routine"; common words are rejected. Empty list clears.

set_name.description: Rename the domain. Names must be unique; rejected if another domain already uses it.

set_sticky.description: true = always inject this domain into context every turn; false = routed only when relevant. Use sticky sparingly.

set_triggers.description: Replace tool triggers: comma-separated name fragments that auto-load this domain whenever you use a tool whose name contains one (substring, case-insensitive). E.g. "mail,github"; for an MCP server use its name ("github" matches mcp_github_*). Empty string clears.

bob.name: cogmem_explain
bob.description: Summarize the status, origin, and evidence of a domain or memory id.

id.description: A domain id (d…) or memory id (h…).

bob.name: cogmem_export
bob.description: Dump the agent's entire memory — every domain and memory, with all their fields — to files/MEMORY_EXPORT.yaml, and report the path and counts. The format can be read back in, so it works as a backup or to hand your memory to another assistant.

bob.name: cogmem_memory_attach
bob.description: Attach a markdown file to an existing memory, or detach the current one. The attached file's FULL contents load into your context whenever that memory does. Use this to point a memory at a different document (e.g. the file moved or was rewritten) or to remove the document while keeping the memory — memory text itself is not editable; retire and re-create for that.

file.description: Path to a markdown file you can read with the file tools (e.g. "files/voice.md", "maestro/style-guide.md"). Omit or pass an empty string to detach the current file.

bob.name: cogmem_memory_create
bob.description: Record a memory. With NO domain_id and NO domain_hint it records to your sticky 'General' domain (always in context). Give a domain_hint to use (or create) a topic domain by name, or a domain_id to target a specific one. Choose the type carefully — it decides whether the memory is in your context every turn or only reachable by search.

domain_hint.description: A domain name: an existing domain with that name is reused, otherwise a new (non-sticky) one is created. Omit to use General.

domain_id.description: Target domain id. If omitted and no domain_hint is given, records to the sticky General domain.

file.description: Optional path to a markdown file (e.g. "files/voice.md", "maestro/style-guide.md") whose FULL contents are injected into your context whenever this memory is in context. Use it for reference material too long to put in the memory text, such as a writing-voice description; keep the memory text as a one-line description of what the document is and when to use it. The path must be one you can read with the file tools, and the file is read fresh each turn.

type.description: fact = something true that stays true. preference = how the user likes things done. rule = a hard directive governing your output or behaviour toward the user. operational = your OWN housekeeping: where you file things, how you work, a rule you set for your own method. event = something that happened at a point in time (a trip, a delivery, a scheduled run, a status as of a date). Use event for anything with a timestamp or that will be stale next week — events are NEVER loaded into your context and are reached only by memory_search, which is what keeps recurring notes from crowding out everything else.

bob.name: cogmem_memory_forget
bob.description: Retire all active memories matching a query (optionally limited to one domain). Reports how many were retired.

query.description: Substring to match against active memory text.

bob.name: cogmem_memory_retire
bob.description: Retire a memory so it is no longer used (it stays in the audit history). To change a memory, retire the old one and create a new one.

bob.name: cogmem_memory_search
bob.description: Search your active memories by a word or phrase in their text (case-insensitive). Use it to look something up when the answer may be in memory but is not currently shown in your context. Event memories are excluded unless you pass include_events — they are never in your context, so search is the ONLY way to reach them.

include_events.description: Include event memories (things that happened at a point in time: trips, deliveries, scheduled runs). Default false. Set true when the question is about the past — "when did we last…", "what happened on…".

query.description: Word or phrase to match against memory text.

bob.name: cogmem_status
bob.description: Report memory status: database path, the last background update, and how many domains and memories are held.

bob.name: common_delete
bob.description: Delete a file from the shared common directory.

name.description: File name (or relative path) within the common directory to delete.

bob.name: common_get
bob.description: Copy a file from the shared common directory into this agent's workspace files/ directory.

as.description: Optional destination name (relative path) under the workspace files/ directory. Defaults to the source basename.

name.description: File name (or relative path) within the common directory to copy.

bob.name: common_list
bob.description: List files in the shared common directory (optionally under a subdir).

subdir.description: Optional subdirectory under the common directory to list.

bob.name: common_put
bob.description: Copy a file from this agent's workspace into the shared common directory.

as.description: Optional destination name (relative path) within the common directory. Defaults to the source basename.

path.description: Relative path within the agent workspace to copy into the common directory.

bob.name: file_append
bob.description: Append content to the end of a file (parent directories created as needed)

backup.description: If true and the target file exists, copy it to <file>.NNNN (next unused 4-digit suffix, starting at 0001) before modification. Silently skipped when the target does not exist.

display.description: If true, after the operation, send the written/edited/appended content to the user as a fenced block separated by `---` markers.

path.description: The file path to append to

bob.name: file_copy
bob.description: Copy a file from source_path to destination_path (parent directories created as needed). Preserves source file mode. Refuses directories.

destination_path.description: Workspace-relative path to copy the file to.

display.description: If true, after the operation, send the copied content to the user as a fenced block separated by `---` markers.

overwrite.description: If true, replace destination when it exists. If false (default), error when destination exists.

source_path.description: Workspace-relative path of the file to copy.

bob.name: file_count
bob.description: Count the lines, words, characters and bytes in a file, like the Unix `wc` command. Use this to size a file before reading it, or to check whether it changed. Counts match wc exactly: `lines` is the number of newline characters, so a file whose last line has no trailing newline reports one fewer than you might count by eye — `final_newline` in the result tells you which case you are in. `characters` counts Unicode characters and `bytes` counts bytes; they differ for non-ASCII text. The file is streamed, so this works on files too large to read.

path.description: Path to the file to count, relative to the workspace.

bob.name: file_delete
bob.description: Delete a file (files only; remove folders with file_rmdir), or a link (the link itself is removed, its target is not touched). Requires sure=true. Makes no backup, and refuses to delete backup files (<name>.NNNN).

path.description: Path of the file to delete.

sure.description: Must be true to confirm deletion.

bob.name: file_delete_bytes
bob.description: Delete bytes start..end (0-based, inclusive). Omit end to delete just the start byte; pass end="end" for end of file.

backup.description: Copy the file to <file>.NNNN before modifying.

display.description: Also show the affected content to the user.

end.description: Last byte (0-based, inclusive). Omit to affect only the start byte; pass "end" for end of file.

path.description: File to modify.

bob.name: file_delete_lines
bob.description: Remove lines by number: deletes lines start..end (1-based). Omit end to delete just the start line; pass end="end" for end of file.

backup.description: Copy the file to <file>.NNNN before modifying.

display.description: Also show the affected content to the user.

end.description: Last line (1-based, inclusive). Omit to affect only the start line; pass "end" for end of file.

path.description: File to modify.

bob.name: file_edit
bob.description: Change text in a file: replaces old_text with new_text. old_text must appear exactly once, exactly as in the file (copy it from file_read_lines).

backup.description: If true and the target file exists, copy it to <file>.NNNN (next unused 4-digit suffix, starting at 0001) before modification. Silently skipped when the target does not exist.

display.description: If true, after the operation, send the written/edited/appended content to the user as a fenced block separated by `---` markers.

old_text.description: The exact text to find and replace

path.description: The file path to edit

bob.name: file_edit_bytes
bob.description: Replace bytes start..end (0-based, inclusive) with `replace`. Omit end to replace just the start byte; pass end="end" for end of file. To remove bytes use file_delete_bytes.

backup.description: Copy the file to <file>.NNNN before modifying.

display.description: Also show the affected content to the user.

end.description: Last byte (0-based, inclusive). Omit to affect only the start byte; pass "end" for end of file.

path.description: File to modify.

replace.description: Replacement content (non-empty; use file_delete_bytes to remove).

bob.name: file_edit_lines
bob.description: Change lines by number: replaces lines start..end (1-based) with `replace`. Omit end to replace just the start line; pass end="end" for end of file. To remove lines use file_delete_lines.

backup.description: Copy the file to <file>.NNNN before modifying.

display.description: Also show the affected content to the user.

end.description: Last line (1-based, inclusive). Omit to affect only the start line; pass "end" for end of file.

path.description: File to modify.

replace.description: Replacement content (non-empty; use file_delete_lines to remove).

bob.name: file_glob
bob.description: Find files by name pattern, e.g. **/*.go or src/**/test_*.py. Searches under path (default: all workspace folders you can read). Returns matching file paths, newest first, at most 200. Folders whose name starts with a dot (.git) are skipped. To find text inside files, use file_search_lines.

path.description: Folder to search under, relative to the workspace or absolute. Default: all workspace folders you can read, with the pattern matched from the workspace (files/**/*.md).

pattern.description: Glob matched against each file's path below `path`: * matches within one folder, ** any number of folders (**/*.go finds Go files everywhere), ? one character, {a,b} either.

bob.name: file_insert_bytes
bob.description: Insert `text` at a byte offset (0 = top of file). Nothing is removed.

at_offset.description: Insert at this 0-based byte offset (0 = top of file).

backup.description: Copy the file to <file>.NNNN before modifying.

display.description: Also show the affected content to the user.

path.description: File to modify.

bob.name: file_insert_lines
bob.description: Add lines without removing any: inserts `text` after a line number (0 = top of file).

after_line.description: Insert after this 1-based line (0 = top of file).

backup.description: Copy the file to <file>.NNNN before modifying.

display.description: Also show the affected content to the user.

path.description: File to modify.

bob.name: file_list
bob.description: See what is in a folder: lists its files and subfolders, one level by default; recursive=true lists the whole tree. To find files by name, use file_glob.

path.description: Path to list

recursive.description: List the entire tree under path (paths shown relative to the workspace). Hidden directories are skipped. Default false (one level).

bob.name: file_mkdir
bob.description: Create a folder, and any missing parent folders. Succeeds if the folder already exists.

path.description: Path of the folder to create.

bob.name: file_move
bob.description: Move a file or a folder from source_path to destination_path to organize files (parent directories created as needed; works across mount boundaries; no content enters context).

destination_path.description: New path for the file or folder.

overwrite.description: Replace destination if it exists (default false). For a folder, its files are merged into the existing destination folder.

source_path.description: Path of the file or folder to move.

bob.name: file_read_bytes
bob.description: Read a file by BYTE offset. Pass `offset` and optional `length` to read a byte range; the status block tells you the next `offset`. Best for binary or very large files. Byte offsets from file_search_bytes feed directly into this tool. (For human-readable line addressing, use file_read_lines.)

length.description: Maximum number of bytes to read.

offset.description: Byte offset to start reading from.

path.description: Path to the file to read.

bob.name: file_read_lines
bob.description: Read the lines you found: reads a file by line number from `start_line` (1-based; a line number from file_search_lines) for `line_count` lines. Lines come back numbered and the status block gives the next `start_line`. Use it to get the exact text before file_edit. (To page by raw bytes instead, use file_read_bytes.)

line_count.description: Number of lines to read from start_line (default 250). Still capped to the byte limit.

path.description: Path to the file to read.

bob.name: file_rmdir
bob.description: Remove a folder (folders only; delete files with file_delete), or a link (the link itself is removed, its target is not touched). Requires sure=true. Removes only an empty folder unless recursive=true. Makes no backup, and refuses to remove backup files (<name>.NNNN).

path.description: Path of the folder to remove.

recursive.description: Also remove everything inside the folder (default false).

sure.description: Must be true to confirm removal.

bob.name: file_search_bytes
bob.description: Search file contents and return each match's BYTE position (start–end) and a snippet — like grep with byte offsets. Pass a match's start byte as `offset` to `file_read_bytes` to read from there. Use this when you page files by bytes; for human-readable line references use `file_search_lines` instead. Searches a single file or a directory tree (recursively). Literal, case-insensitive match by default; set regex=true for a regular expression.

path.description: File or directory to search (directories are searched recursively). Defaults to the workspace root.

query.description: Text to find (literal substring, case-insensitive) or a regular expression when regex=true.

regex.description: Treat query as a regular expression (case-sensitive as written). Default false.

bob.name: file_search_lines
bob.description: Find text in files: returns matching lines with their path and line number, like grep. Then read around a match with file_read_lines (start_line = the line number). Searches one file or a folder and everything below it (default: all workspace folders you can read), skipping files .gitignore ignores. Literal, case-insensitive by default; regex=true for a regular expression. To find files by name, use file_glob.

context.description: Lines to show before and after each match (default 0, max 10). A result shows at most 2000 lines.

include.description: Only search files whose path matches this glob, e.g. *.go or src/**/*.ts. A pattern without / matches the file name in any folder; with no path, one with / matches paths from the workspace (files/**/*.go).

max_results.description: Maximum matches to return, or files with output=files or count (default 50, max 200).

output.description: lines (default): the matching lines; files: only the paths of files that match; count: the number of matching lines in each file.

path.description: File or folder to search (folders are searched recursively), relative to the workspace or absolute. Default: all workspace folders you can read.

query.description: Text to find (literal substring, case-insensitive) or a regular expression when regex=true.

regex.description: Treat query as a regular expression (case-sensitive as written). Default false.

bob.name: file_view_image
bob.description: View an image file so you can actually see it (requires a vision-capable model). Reads an image from the workspace (png, jpeg, gif, webp) and attaches it for you to look at — use this instead of file_read_lines/file_read_bytes, which return unusable binary for images. Large images are automatically downscaled. Max source size 10 MB.

focus.description: Optional: what to look for / the question to answer about the image.

path.description: Path to the image file, relative to the workspace (or an allowed absolute path).

bob.name: file_write
bob.description: Create a file, or replace a whole file: writes content (parent folders created as needed). Refuses to replace an existing file unless overwrite is true. To change part of a file, use file_edit.

backup.description: If true and the target file exists, copy it to <file>.NNNN (next unused 4-digit suffix, starting at 0001) before modification. Silently skipped when the target does not exist.

content.description: Content to write to the file

display.description: If true, after the operation, send the written/edited/appended content to the user as a fenced block separated by `---` markers.

overwrite.description: If the target file already exists and overwrite is not true, the call fails. Set overwrite: true to replace an existing file.

path.description: Path to the file to write

bob.name: msg_send
bob.description: Send a message to the user in the current conversation. Use this when you want to say something to the user.

bob.name: msg_send_file
bob.description: Send files to the chat you are answering. You can only send files you're allowed to read with the file tools.

files.description: The files to send, in order (1 to 10).

filename.description: Name the chat shows. Defaults to the file's own name.

path.description: Path of the file, as the file tools take it.

bob.name: search_tools
bob.description: Search for available tools by capability. Returns matching tool names with one-line descriptions and makes those tools available: call one directly, or call get_tool_details on a name to see its full schema. Natural-language query by default; set regex:true to match a regular expression if the natural-language search can't find the tool. Discoverable tool groups: ccv3.

query.description: What you want to do (natural language), or a regex pattern when regex is true.

regex.description: Treat query as a regex over tool name/description instead of a natural-language search.

bob.name: session_clear
bob.description: Clear your active conversation and start fresh. Long-term memory is preserved — past messages stay retrievable via session_messages / session_search and past summaries via session_summary_get. Use between unrelated short tasks to reset working context. Pass an optional `message` as a handoff note to your fresh self (e.g. the next task to do). After calling this, stop and end your turn: the clear happens at the turn boundary and a new turn begins with your handoff.

message.description: Optional handoff note delivered to you on the fresh turn after the clear — e.g. the next task or relevant context.

bob.name: session_compact
bob.description: Trigger an immediate context compaction for the current session. Use after completing a major task to summarise prior messages and free context window space. The result returns the compaction report and the new summary now in your context; pass an optional `message` to append a note to yourself (e.g. what to do next).

message.description: Optional note appended to the result — e.g. a reminder of what to do next after compaction.

bob.name: session_info
bob.description: Return metadata about the current session: session key, start time, channel, message count, archive sequence range, and the seq range covered by the current summary. Use to orient yourself after a context compression or to understand how much history is available.

bob.name: session_messages
bob.description: Retrieve historical messages from the current session archive by sequence number. Returns messages in the requested seq range, capped to the most recent 5000. Request smaller ranges for efficiency. Use when the context summary references a seq number and you need the full message content.

seq.description: Single message sequence number. Takes precedence over seq_start/seq_end.

seq_end.description: End of sequence range (inclusive). Used when seq is absent.

seq_start.description: Start of sequence range (inclusive). Used when seq is absent.

bob.name: session_search
bob.description: Search archived session messages using FTS5 full-text search. FTS5 syntax examples: cat AND dog, "exact phrase", cat OR dog, NOT cat, cat*, NEAR(cat dog, 5). Default 20 results, maximum 100. Role filter values: "user", "assistant", "tool". Omit for all roles. Use when you need to find past messages by topic rather than by sequence number. Maximum query length: 500 characters.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default 20, maximum 100.

query.description: FTS5 search expression. Supports AND, OR, NOT, phrase queries ("exact phrase"), prefix (word*), and NEAR(cat dog, 5). Maximum 500 characters.

role.description: Filter results by role: "user", "assistant", or "tool". Omit to return all roles.

bob.name: session_summary_get
bob.description: Retrieve the full text of one context-summary checkpoint for the current session by id. Use session_summary_list to discover available ids. Returns the summary rendered as Markdown (goals, progress, pending, constraints, key moments) with the message sequence references it cites.

id.description: The checkpoint id to retrieve (from session_summary_list).

bob.name: session_summary_list
bob.description: List the context-summary checkpoints recorded for the current session. Each entry shows its id, the covered message sequence range, when it was generated, and the model that produced it. Use session_summary_get with an id to read the full summary. Newest checkpoints have the highest ids.

limit.description: Maximum number of checkpoints to return (most recent first). Omit for all.

offset.description: Number of most-recent checkpoints to skip before listing. Default 0.

bob.name: time_now
bob.description: Get the current date, time, and timezone. The system prompt carries today's date only, so call this whenever you need the time of day, the timezone or UTC offset, or a precise timestamp — for example to work out how long until something, or to convert between zones.

timezone.description: Optional IANA timezone name (e.g. "America/Toronto", "UTC"). Defaults to the server's local timezone.

bob.name: web_fetch
bob.description: Fetch a URL and extract readable content (HTML to text). Use this to get weather info, news, articles, or any web content.

bob.name: web_search
bob.description: Search the web for current information. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets from search results.

carol.name: cogmem_consolidate
carol.description: Ask the background process to review the recent conversation and update memory now. Returns immediately; the work runs in the background.

carol.name: cogmem_domain_archive
carol.description: Archive a domain so it is no longer used in prompting.

carol.name: cogmem_domain_create
carol.description: Create a new memory domain and return its assigned id. A domain groups related memories; register each ongoing project/topic as its own domain. Names must be unique — creating one with an existing name returns an error (reuse or rename instead).

keyword_triggers.description: Optional keyword triggers: words/phrases that load this domain when they appear in the incoming message (whole-phrase, word-boundary). Prefer multi-word phrases like "morning routine"; common words are rejected. Use this to pull a workflow's context up when a cron job fires.

sticky.description: true = always inject this domain into context every turn (use sparingly). Default false: loaded only when relevant.

triggers.description: Optional tool triggers: comma-separated name fragments that auto-load this domain whenever you use a tool whose name contains one (substring, case-insensitive). E.g. "mail,github"; for an MCP server use its name ("github" matches mcp_github_*).

carol.name: cogmem_domain_get
carol.description: Load a domain by id, with its active memories as readable text (each memory's id included).

carol.name: cogmem_domain_list
carol.description: List memory domains (id, name, summary, status; sticky ones are marked). Optionally filter by status. To see everything you're tracking, list with no filter.

carol.name: cogmem_domain_migrate
carol.description: Merge two domains: move every memory from the 'from' domain into the 'to' domain, then permanently delete the 'from' domain. Use this to consolidate duplicate/overlapping domains into one.

from.description: Source domain id — its memories are moved out and the domain is deleted.

to.description: Destination domain id — receives the moved memories.

carol.name: cogmem_domain_update
carol.description: Update a domain — a patch: pass only the fields you want to change (rename, summary, state, sticky, triggers). No version needed.

set_keyword_triggers.description: Replace keyword triggers: words/phrases that load this domain when they appear in the incoming message (whole-phrase, word-boundary). This is the full list domain_get shows, including keyword triggers added automatically; leave one out to remove it. Prefer multi-word phrases like "morning routine"; common words are rejected. Empty list clears.

set_name.description: Rename the domain. Names must be unique; rejected if another domain already uses it.

set_sticky.description: true = always inject this domain into context every turn; false = routed only when relevant. Use sticky sparingly.

set_triggers.description: Replace tool triggers: comma-separated name fragments that auto-load this domain whenever you use a tool whose name contains one (substring, case-insensitive). E.g. "mail,github"; for an MCP server use its name ("github" matches mcp_github_*). Empty string clears.

carol.name: cogmem_explain
carol.description: Summarize the status, origin, and evidence of a domain or memory id.

id.description: A domain id (d…) or memory id (h…).

carol.name: cogmem_export
carol.description: Dump the agent's entire memory — every domain and memory, with all their fields — to files/MEMORY_EXPORT.yaml, and report the path and counts. The format can be read back in, so it works as a backup or to hand your memory to another assistant.

carol.name: cogmem_memory_attach
carol.description: Attach a markdown file to an existing memory, or detach the current one. The attached file's FULL contents load into your context whenever that memory does. Use this to point a memory at a different document (e.g. the file moved or was rewritten) or to remove the document while keeping the memory — memory text itself is not editable; retire and re-create for that.

file.description: Path to a markdown file you can read with the file tools (e.g. "files/voice.md", "maestro/style-guide.md"). Omit or pass an empty string to detach the current file.

carol.name: cogmem_memory_create
carol.description: Record a memory. With NO domain_id and NO domain_hint it records to your sticky 'General' domain (always in context). Give a domain_hint to use (or create) a topic domain by name, or a domain_id to target a specific one. Choose the type carefully — it decides whether the memory is in your context every turn or only reachable by search.

domain_hint.description: A domain name: an existing domain with that name is reused, otherwise a new (non-sticky) one is created. Omit to use General.

domain_id.description: Target domain id. If omitted and no domain_hint is given, records to the sticky General domain.

file.description: Optional path to a markdown file (e.g. "files/voice.md", "maestro/style-guide.md") whose FULL contents are injected into your context whenever this memory is in context. Use it for reference material too long to put in the memory text, such as a writing-voice description; keep the memory text as a one-line description of what the document is and when to use it. The path must be one you can read with the file tools, and the file is read fresh each turn.

type.description: fact = something true that stays true. preference = how the user likes things done. rule = a hard directive governing your output or behaviour toward the user. operational = your OWN housekeeping: where you file things, how you work, a rule you set for your own method. event = something that happened at a point in time (a trip, a delivery, a scheduled run, a status as of a date). Use event for anything with a timestamp or that will be stale next week — events are NEVER loaded into your context and are reached only by memory_search, which is what keeps recurring notes from crowding out everything else.

carol.name: cogmem_memory_forget
carol.description: Retire all active memories matching a query (optionally limited to one domain). Reports how many were retired.

query.description: Substring to match against active memory text.

carol.name: cogmem_memory_retire
carol.description: Retire a memory so it is no longer used (it stays in the audit history). To change a memory, retire the old one and create a new one.

carol.name: cogmem_memory_search
carol.description: Search your active memories by a word or phrase in their text (case-insensitive). Use it to look something up when the answer may be in memory but is not currently shown in your context. Event memories are excluded unless you pass include_events — they are never in your context, so search is the ONLY way to reach them.

include_events.description: Include event memories (things that happened at a point in time: trips, deliveries, scheduled runs). Default false. Set true when the question is about the past — "when did we last…", "what happened on…".

query.description: Word or phrase to match against memory text.

carol.name: cogmem_status
carol.description: Report memory status: database path, the last background update, and how many domains and memories are held.

carol.name: file_read_lines
carol.description: Read the lines you found: reads a file by line number from `start_line` (1-based; a line number from file_search_lines) for `line_count` lines. Lines come back numbered and the status block gives the next `start_line`. Use it to get the exact text before file_edit. (To page by raw bytes instead, use file_read_bytes.)

line_count.description: Number of lines to read from start_line (default 250). Still capped to the byte limit.

path.description: Path to the file to read.

carol.name: get_tool_details
carol.description: Show the full input schema of a tool found via search_tools. Pass the exact tool name from the search results.

name.description: Exact tool name from search_tools results.

carol.name: search_tools
carol.description: Search for available tools by capability. Returns matching tool names with one-line descriptions and makes those tools available: call one directly, or call get_tool_details on a name to see its full schema. Natural-language query by default; set regex:true to match a regular expression if the natural-language search can't find the tool.

query.description: What you want to do (natural language), or a regex pattern when regex is true.

regex.description: Treat query as a regex over tool name/description instead of a natural-language search.

carol.name: shell_ctrl
carol.description: Manage jobs started by shell_exec. list: your jobs. wait: block until the job ends, a new output line matches until, or seconds pass; returns the new output. input: write text to the job's standard input. stop: end the job, or all your jobs with all. A job's full output is a log file: read it with the file tools.

all.description: stop: stop all your running jobs

raw.description: input: send text exactly as given

text.description: input: text for the job's standard input; a newline is added unless raw

until.description: wait: return when a new output line matches this regular expression

carol.name: shell_exec
carol.description: Run a command-line program: git, builds and tests, and Unix tools such as grep, sed, awk and jq for pipelines. Long output is cut to its head and tail and the full log file is named. A command still running at its timeout is kept as a job; background starts one and returns at once. Manage jobs with shell_ctrl. To find, read or edit files, the file tools are usually better: their output is numbered and limited in size.

background.description: Start as a job and return at once

notify.description: For a job: tell you when it ends

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the command before returning (default 60, at most 600)

working_dir.description: Directory to run in; relative paths start at your workspace. Default: where your previous command ended, else your workspace
